findings.title: Enforce inspection size limits before reading untrusted content into host memory
findings.trigger: An eligible untrusted PR contains large blobs, many changed files, or a diff exceeding MAX_INSPECTION_INPUT_BYTES.
findings.execution_path: _execute_untrusted() calls build_inspection_input() before reserving outputs or entering the container. Both diffs are captured in full, then every changed regular-file blob is captured by _git_bytes(). PER_FILE_CONTENT_LIMIT is checked only afterward. The aggregate limit is calculated after all sections are assembled, and _execute_inspection() rejects the input only after prompt rendering and reservation.
findings.consequence: The advertised limits do not bound host memory or extraction work. A large untrusted change can exhaust host resources before an INCOMPLETE status is recorded; Docker resource limits do not protect this pre-container path. Even an already-oversized diff causes further blob reads and prompt allocation.
findings.evidence: A mocked command-runner reproduction supplied oversized diffs and one oversized blob. build_inspection_input() still fetched the blob and returned 3,000,166 retained text bytes with oversize=true. Existing tests verify omission/rejection after extraction, but do not assert bounded reads or early termination. Host OOM itself was not induced.
findings.suggested_fix: Check blob sizes with git cat-file -s before fetching contents. Stream diff output with a hard byte budget and terminate extraction when it is exceeded. Enforce a cumulative budget while collecting file sections, and record INCOMPLETE without rendering or persisting the oversized prompt. Add regression assertions that oversized blobs are never fetched and no further extraction occurs after budget exhaustion.

limitations: Did not independently run pytest in the read-only sandbox. The supplied harness evidence identifies the exact inspected head and reports exit 0, 3145 passed, 1 skipped, and 38 warnings.
Did not run live Docker, authentication, GitHub, or post-merge end-to-end verification.
The resource-limit defect was reproduced with an injected command runner; actual host memory exhaustion was not attempted.
Some large read outputs were truncated by the tool; affected sections were inspected through subsequent targeted reads.
The initial reproduction heredoc failed under sandbox restrictions; the equivalent in-memory invocation succeeded.
